scope_note: Six independently researched, evidence-reviewed candidates were synthesized without adding or padding entries. The scope compares open-source/self-hosted products against So7ob use cases: single-provider appointment booking, resource reservation, service/rental marketplace, and field-service dispatch. All recommendations remain reference_only; scores are screening signals, not adoption approval or a universal ranking.

records.name: Cal.diy (Cal.com community edition)
records.category: Appointment scheduling infrastructure for service providers and teams
records.fit_limitations: Strong fit as an individual-provider scheduling subsystem: event types, recurring/seated events, availability, booking management, calendar/conferencing connectors, paid events, embeds and webhooks. Poor fit as a marketplace: no provider discovery/catalog, marketplace onboarding/moderation/search/ranking, commissions/split settlement/escrow, or buyer-provider network. Cal.diy explicitly removes Teams, organizations, round-robin/collective team event types, SSO/SAML, SCIM, workflows, routing forms, insights and other enterprise features. Do not count Cal.com commercial hosted/enterprise features as community-edition support.
records.license_caveats: MIT License is present in the canonical LICENSE file and GitHub reports MIT. Standard notice-retention and warranty-disclaimer terms apply; legal review remains necessary for third-party dependencies, trademarks/branding, and So7ob distribution/deployment facts.
records.maintenance_security: Repository is not archived; observed HEAD 54343aa685ae8f33159d2f485ec4a57bad5c574a is dated 2026-09-20. Latest observed tagged release is v6.2.0, published 2026-03-01, so main is active but release lag and absence of visible supported-branch/SLA evidence reduce production confidence. SECURITY.md gives security@cal.com disclosure guidance and a three-business-day response target; a recursive Yarn npm-audit workflow fails on critical vulnerabilities, but a clean current audit was not independently reproduced. Open issues #29955, #29956 and #29957 report allow-all permission checks/unauthorized team mutations and an IDOR-style missing membership check; they were not independently exploited but are specific, material and unresolved in the observed state. Official docs warn about self-hosting sensitive data and unsafe TLS workarounds. The project is explicitly recommended for personal, non-production use and has no hosted/managed Cal.diy.
records.interoperability: Official comparison lists Google, Outlook/Office 365, Apple, CalDAV, Lark, Feishu, Zoho, Exchange and ICS calendars; Daily/Zoom/Meet/Teams/Webex/Jitsi and others; webhooks, Zapier, n8n/Make/Pipedream, CRM, messaging and analytics connectors; embeds; API v2 REST, API keys and platform/OAuth clients. API v2 and platform READMEs document Nest.js, OAuth clients, redirect URIs, tests and Swagger generation files. Provider credentials, connector readiness and marketplace settlement behavior require separate validation.
records.arabic_rtl: Arabic is an explicit target locale; packages/i18n/locales/ar/common.json exists with about 4,610 top-level keys, Next i18next loads target locales with English fallback, and an i18n automation workflow exists. Some Tailwind RTL utilities and a platform readingDirection option are present, but no canonical Arabic end-to-end visual/RTL acceptance matrix was verified. Treat Arabic/RTL as partial until booking, availability, payments, email, embeds, admin and mobile flows are tested.

records.name: Easy!Appointments
records.fit_limitations: Strong fit for a self-hosted single-business or team booking component such as salon, consultant, education, event, or other scheduled service workflows. Poor fit as a marketplace foundation: documented resources model providers/services inside one installation, not independent vendors, vendor approval, storefronts, cross-vendor search, commissions, split payments, payouts, disputes, or marketplace checkout. So7ob would need to own those capabilities in a separate marketplace/tenant/payment layer and integrate through the API or a custom fork.
records.license_caveats: GNU GPL v3.0 is explicit in LICENSE, composer.json, package.json, and README; README separately identifies content as CC BY 3.0. Commercial installation is advertised, but GPL obligations, hosted/distribution facts, notices, and third-party assets require legal review. Official premium offerings are managed hosting, installation, upgrades, migration, support, customization, and white-label services; no reviewed evidence establishes a paid plugin catalog or that premium extensions share the core license.
records.maintenance_security: Active and recently maintained: stable 1.6.0 (2026-05-27), 1.6.1-beta.1 (2026-09-07), and main-branch commits through 2026-10-06. Material conflict: main composer.json still declares package version 1.5.2 despite 1.6.x tags, so packaging must use an immutable verified release/tag rather than an unpinned branch. SECURITY.md provides email reporting but no supported-version matrix, public advisory feed, or response SLA. The 1.6.0 changelog records request-method validation, injection, authorization, CalDAV SSRF/internal-network, Google Calendar isolation, privacy, and other security fixes. CI runs PHPUnit but uses composer update rather than a locked install, limiting reproducibility. Require pinned dependency audits, threat modeling, HTTPS/secrets/rate-limit/CAPTCHA/CalDAV-egress checks, and authorization review before production use.
records.interoperability: Documented JSON REST API supports availability, appointments, customers, services, service categories, providers, secretaries, settings, and related resources, using Basic Authentication or a configured Bearer API key; OpenAPI is supplied. Integrations/features include Google Calendar, CalDAV, LDAP/Active Directory, SMTP/email, webhooks, Matomo, Jitsi, Google Meet, ICS, and ALTCHA. API version/backward-compatibility guarantees, webhook retry/signature semantics, payments, marketplace adapters, and tenant-scoped authorization are not verified.
records.arabic_rtl: Internationalization architecture is verified through per-language folders and translation files; an Arabic locale exists with Arabic strings, and the official site claims more than 21 community-maintained languages. Full Arabic completeness and global RTL/bidi behavior are not verified. Code search found a targeted timepicker RTL style but no documented global RTL mode or Arabic layout test. Require Arabic public booking/backend/email/mobile acceptance testing.

records.name: LibreBooking
records.fit_limitations: Good fit for organization-owned rooms, equipment, desks, labs, calendars, appointment slots, quotas, approvals, waitlists, and utilization reporting. Poor/unsupported fit as a two-sided service marketplace because core evidence lacks provider onboarding, provider storefronts, service listings, marketplace discovery/ranking, reviews, merchant/customer workflows, commissions, payouts, or settlement. Retain as reference architecture or internal booking component, not as the marketplace base without substantial product/domain work.
records.license_caveats: GPL-3.0-only in composer.json, with the full GNU GPL version 3 text shipped in LICENSE.md. GPLv3 permits commercial use/charging but imposes copyleft, source, notice, and distribution obligations for covered conveyed works; legal review is required for So7ob modifications, containers, plugins, and distribution/SaaS model.
records.maintenance_security: Strong recent activity: official releases v6.0.0 (2026-10-01), v6.1.0 (2026-10-03), v7.0.0 (2026-10-06), and v7.1.0 (2026-10-13), with security, testing, feature, documentation, and dependency changes. Latest checked develop commit was 2026-10-13. Security support is latest-release-only and the project describes a small volunteer team, creating capacity risk. Critical security history is a gate: all versions before 7.1.0 permit unauthenticated account takeover via forged Remember Me cookies, and versions before 7.0.0 had another critical administrator-takeover vulnerability; fixes are not backported. v7.1.0 removes Remember Me. No independent current dependency audit or exploit reproduction was run.
records.interoperability: Documented JSON-over-HTTP API under /Web/Services/index.php uses an Authenticate call and X-Booked-SessionToken/X-Booked-UserId headers, with routes for core booking entities. OAuth2 and SAML are documented; LDAP/AD and other authentication plugins exist; README claims Outlook/Thunderbird through ICS. SAML explicitly cannot authenticate API methods because it requires browser redirects. Stripe and other dependencies do not prove marketplace checkout, refunds, split payouts, or reconciliation.
records.arabic_rtl: Arabic language file lang/ar.php exists with extensive Arabic strings and inherits English; the locale architecture and user language field are evidenced. Explicit RTL behavior is not evidenced for Arabic: the inspected Arabic constructor does not set TextDirection, while Hebrew explicitly sets rtl. No primary-source evidence of Arabic visual QA, bidi behavior, Arabic date/email/export/accessibility validation was found; treat RTL as unknown, not verified support.

records.name: Cocorico
records.category: Service and rental marketplace with booking/availability flows
records.fit_limitations: Strong historical fit for two-sided service/rental marketplaces requiring listings, availability, booking request/acceptance, time-unit modes, fee/refund semantics, notifications, and admin flows. It is a marketplace product with a booking product embedded, not merely a booking widget. It is not verified as current headless SaaS, API-first software, regulated healthcare/travel product, or maintained commercial service. Optional/bundle-dependent functions include listing search notation, SMS, listing alerts, SEO sitemap generation, and deposit refund jobs. If So7ob opens a fork evaluation, gates are legal review of MIT plus third-party bundles and open-source-vs-Second boundary; supported PHP/Symfony modernization; dependency/SAST/penetration review; isolated SQL/MongoDB deployment with secrets/backups/monitoring; API/webhook/idempotency design; payment-provider regression tests; and Arabic/RTL visual/accessibility tests.
records.license_caveats: MIT, clearly identified in LICENSE and composer.json; repository license grants use, modification, distribution, sublicensing, and sale subject to notice retention. Review third-party bundle licenses and keep the commercial Second service/trademarks outside any assumption of repository rights.
records.maintenance_security: Legacy/reference status. GitHub API says repository is public and not archived but code pushed_at is 2021-10-19; latest commit endpoint shows 2021-02-09. Releases endpoint returns latest v0.15.1 published 2020-07-09, with v0.15.0 in 2019. Branches master and 0.15 point to the 2021 commit; current repo description redirects toward Second. composer.lock exists and legacy docs instruct SensioLabs security:check, but GitHub security page says no security policy detected and no SECURITY.md. CI is an old Travis matrix for PHP 7.1/7.2 that only syntax-lints PHP. Legacy PHP 7.1/Symfony 3.4 dependencies include old Doctrine, MongoDB ODM, Guzzle, HWI OAuth and Sonata Admin packages; current vulnerability exposure and supported security branch are unverified. Fresh dependency/SAST/penetration review is an adoption blocker.
records.interoperability: Primary docs evidence Google Places/Maps/Geocoding, Microsoft Translator, and Facebook Login/OAuth. Source/tests and pricing/cron docs evidence MangoPay-era card, wallet, transfer, bank-wire, and refund flows. No maintained public REST/OpenAPI/Swagger contract was verified; the integration doc is an HTML-to-Twig asset guide, and APIfication remains a roadmap item. Any fork would need API contracts, webhooks/idempotency, provider credential rotation, and current payment compatibility tests.
records.arabic_rtl: Localization evidence is absent for Arabic: no verified Arabic strings, Arabic completeness, bidi/RTL CSS, visual RTL behavior, or Arabic QA. UTF-8 support is not RTL support. Treat Arabic/i18n/RTL as unknown until acceptance tests are passed.

records.name: OpenFieldService
records.category: Field-service job scheduling, technician dispatch and service-business operations
records.fit_limitations: Good reference fit for the service-provider/operator side of a marketplace: scheduling, dispatch, technician workload, work-order state, customer/service history, equipment history, invoicing and field packet UX. Poor fit as So7ob marketplace code because consumer discovery, provider onboarding, public booking, availability search, checkout/payments, commissions, reviews, messaging, customer portal, moderation and tenancy are not verified. Explicitly excluded features include ownership transfers, component hierarchies, support cases, maintenance plans, parts applicability, coverage adjudication, customer portals and telemetry ingestion. No paid plugin/extension ecosystem or commercial SLA/service boundary was substantiated. Adoption gates are legal review, security/identity/tenant controls, marketplace feature build, CI/production operations and Arabic/RTL implementation.
records.license_caveats: Current repository LICENSE is MIT and GitHub metadata reports SPDX MIT. Historical issue #17 documented an AGPL-3.0 README footer versus MIT LICENSE mismatch; merged PR #18 corrected the README to MIT and linked it to LICENSE on 2026-09-23. Retain the correction history and perform dependency/license legal review before redistribution.
records.maintenance_security: Early but active: checked main commit 817a8699cb8ce49872dc737a0e14a4f7bc2d920a was signed and dated 2026-10-06, with meaningful recent commits for offline access, customer history and booking UX. Repository metadata shows created 2026-04-04, pushed 2026-10-06, not archived, one open issue, no tags and no GitHub releases. No supported-branch policy, release cadence or SLA is documented. No SECURITY.md, advisory policy, Dependabot, security-scanning workflow or documented auth/authorization/rate-limit/tenant-isolation controls were found. Offline browser caching stores customer details, so production use needs a privacy/security threat model and operational controls. No vulnerability audit was performed.
records.interoperability: Documented REST/OpenAPI endpoints cover stats, jobs, customers, sites, equipment/assets, technicians, service types, materials, invoices, notes and checklists; UUIDs are used and README/agent.md show curl use. No maintained payment, calendar, maps/routing, messaging, identity-provider, CRM/ERP, webhook or marketplace connectors are documented. No API versioning, auth contract, SDK, webhook contract or rate-limit policy is verified.
records.arabic_rtl: No Arabic coverage, locale switching, translation files, i18n framework or RTL/bidi behavior was found in the checked repository tree or documented guides; visible UI copy is English. Treat localization as absent at implementation level and requiring deliberate extraction, Arabic translation and RTL/mobile layout testing, not configuration-only work.

records.name: Beveren Field Service Management
records.category: ERPNext/Frappe field-service management extension with internal service requests, quotations, orders, appointments, dispatch, technician scheduling, parts, and invoicing; not a consumer booking marketplace
records.fit_limitations: Good reference for internal provider back-office scheduling/dispatch and ERPNext service lifecycle. Appointment booking is an ERP document created from service orders and assigned to known technicians, not public marketplace booking. Missing or unverified marketplace capabilities include consumer/provider onboarding, multi-vendor catalog/discovery, public availability search, checkout/payments, payouts, reviews, refunds/disputes, notifications, and marketplace settlement. README install alias beveren_fsm redirects to this repo, but the separate beveren_fsm_spa development repo returned 404, reducing reproducibility. Use as architecture/reference material, not as the So7ob marketplace code base.
records.license_caveats: Repository contains GNU AGPL v3 (19 Nov 2007) and GitHub identifies AGPL-3.0, but beveren_fsm/hooks.py says app_license=mit and root package.json says ISC. Treat AGPL as governing pending legal review; hosted use, modifications, integrations, and distribution require assessment of AGPL obligations.
records.maintenance_security: Active but early: develop is the default/protected branch; recent meaningful commits include a 2026-09-20 smoke-test/UI change and GitHub metadata showed October 2026 updates. Repository metadata showed 24 stars and one open issue. There are no GitHub releases or documented stable supported branch. GitHub reports no SECURITY.md policy and no published security advisories. CI runs pre-commit plus a Bench/MariaDB/Redis integration job, but tolerates absent tests; root npm test is a failing placeholder. Python/Frappe dependencies are not pinned in pyproject, frontend has many third-party dependencies and date-fns=latest, and geocoding depends on public Nominatim with simple in-memory throttling. Security posture is unverified and requires review.
records.interoperability: Whitelisted Frappe APIs cover user profile/language, geocoding, unassigned orders, appointment create/update, bulk technician assignment/removal, appointment retrieval/statuses, and invoice lookup. SPA uses session credentials/CSRF and includes frappe-react-sdk. No OpenAPI schema, versioned public API, webhooks, payment/payout connector, OAuth client flow, or marketplace-provider connectors are documented. Nominatim/OSM is the only clearly evidenced external service integration.
records.arabic_rtl: Partial, not production-verified. Settings offers English and Arabic (العربية), persists user language, and sets document/body direction to RTL for Arabic. No evidence of full translated message catalogs, Arabic coverage across the domain UI, bidi-aware component tests, Arabic date/number/currency testing, or RTL regression screenshots.
